71: pub async fn discover_jwks_uri(http: &reqwest::Client, issuer: &str) -> Result<String, JwtError> {
72:     let url = format!("{issuer}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server");
73:     let meta: Value = http
74:         .get(&url)
75:         .send()
76:         .await
77:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Transport(e.to_string()))?
78:         .error_for_status()
79:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Discovery(e.to_string()))?
80:         .json()
81:         .await
82:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Discovery(e.to_string()))?;
83:     meta.get("jwks_uri")
84:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
85:         .map(|s| s.to_string())
86:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Discovery("metadata missing jwks_uri".into()))
87: }
88: 
89: /// Fetch the JWKS document.
90: pub async fn fetch_jwks(http: &reqwest::Client, jwks_uri: &str) -> Result<Value, JwtError> {
91:     http.get(jwks_uri)
92:         .send()
93:         .await
94:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Transport(e.to_string()))?
95:         .error_for_status()
96:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Jwks(e.to_string()))?
97:         .json()
98:         .await
99:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Jwks(e.to_string()))
100: }
101: 
102: /// Convert an RSA JWK (n, e) into a jsonwebtoken DecodingKey.
103: ///
104: /// Mirrors the proven pattern in `mcp-server/src/oauth.rs`: decode base64url
105: /// big-endian integers, pad the modulus to a multiple of 128 bytes, build the
106: /// RSA public key, and export to SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
107: fn jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk: &Value) -> Result<DecodingKey, JwtError> {
108:     if jwk.get("kty").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) != Some("RSA") {
109:         return Err(JwtError::Jwks("unsupported key type, expected RSA".into()));
110:     }
111:     let n = jwk
112:         .get("n")
113:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
114:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("missing n".into()))?;
115:     let e = jwk
116:         .get("e")
117:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
118:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("missing e".into()))?;
119:     let engine = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD;
120:     let n_bytes = engine
121:         .decode(n)
122:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("bad n: {err}")))?;
123:     let e_bytes = engine
124:         .decode(e)
125:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("bad e: {err}")))?;
126: 
127:     let key_size_bytes = ((n_bytes.len() + 127) / 128) * 128;
128:     let n_padded = if n_bytes.len() < key_size_bytes {
129:         let mut padded = vec![0u8; key_size_bytes - n_bytes.len()];
130:         padded.extend_from_slice(&n_bytes);
131:         padded
132:     } else {
133:         n_bytes
134:     };
135: 
136:     let n_big = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&n_padded);
137:     let e_big = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&e_bytes);
138:     let rsa_pub = rsa::RsaPublicKey::new(n_big, e_big)
139:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("rsa key: {err}")))?;
140:     let pem = rsa_pub
141:         .to_public_key_pem(rsa::pkcs8::LineEnding::default())
142:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("pem: {err}")))?;
143:     DecodingKey::from_rsa_pem(pem.as_bytes())
144:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("decoding key: {err}")))
145: }
146: 
147: /// Validate a JWT access token against the issuer and the exact resource audience.
148: ///
149: /// Checks: signature (via discovery JWKS), `iss`, `aud` (contains the exact
150: /// resource), `exp`, and extracts the standard claims.
151: pub async fn validate_access_token(
152:     http: &reqwest::Client,
153:     token: &str,
154:     issuer: &str,
155:     resource: &str,
156: ) -> Result<AccessClaims, JwtError> {
157:     let jwks_uri = discover_jwks_uri(http, issuer).await?;
158:     let jwks = fetch_jwks(http, &jwks_uri).await?;
159:     let keys = jwks
160:         .get("keys")
161:         .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
162:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("no keys".into()))?;
163: 
164:     // Decode header to find kid + alg.
165:     let header = jsonwebtoken::decode_header(token)
166:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Token(format!("header: {err}")))?;
167:     let kid = header.kid;
168:     let alg = header.alg;
169: 
170:     let jwk = keys
171:         .iter()
172:         .find(|k| k.get("kid").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) == kid.as_deref())
173:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks(format!("no key for kid {kid:?}")))?;
174: 
175:     let decoding_key = jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk)?;
176: 
177:     let mut validation = Validation::new(alg);
178:     validation.set_issuer(&[issuer]);
179:     validation.set_audience(&[resource]);
180:     validation.leeway = 30;
181: 
182:     let data = jsonwebtoken::decode::<AccessClaims>(token, &decoding_key, &validation)
183:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Token(err.to_string()))?;
184:     Ok(data.claims)
185: }

48:     /// Extract the OAuth bearer token from the request Authorization header.
49:     fn extract_bearer_token(
50:         headers: &axum::http::HeaderMap,
51:     ) -> Result<String, axum::http::Response<axum::body::Body>> {
52:         let auth_header = headers
53:             .get(axum::http::header::AUTHORIZATION)
54:             .ok_or_else(|| unauthorized_response(None, "missing authorization header"))?;
55: 
56:         let auth_str = auth_header
57:             .to_str()
58:             .map_err(|_| unauthorized_response(None, "invalid authorization header encoding"))?;
59: 
60:         if !auth_str.starts_with("Bearer ") {
61:             return Err(unauthorized_response(
62:                 None,
63:                 "authorization must use Bearer scheme",
64:             ));
65:         }
66: 
67:         let token = &auth_str[7..];
68:         if token.is_empty() {
69:             return Err(unauthorized_response(None, "empty bearer token"));
70:         }
71: 
72:         Ok(token.to_string())
73:     }

103:     /// Handle an incoming MCP request.
104:     ///
105:     /// This is the entry point for all MCP protocol communication.
106:     /// It validates the OAuth token, dispatches to the appropriate tool,
107:     /// records the invocation in the local audit log, and returns a
108:     /// structured MCP response.
109:     pub async fn handle_mcp_request(
110:         &self,
111:         request_id: String,
112:         request: axum::http::Request<axum::body::Body>,
113:     ) -> axum::http::Response<axum::body::Body> {
114:         // Check Origin/CORS
115:         if !self.check_origin(&request) {
116:             return axum::http::Response::builder()
117:                 .status(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN)
118:                 .body(axum::body::Body::from(
119:                     serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
120:                         "error": {
121:                             "code": -2001,
122:                             "message": "origin not allowed",
123:                         },
124:                     }))
125:                     .unwrap(),
126:                 ))
127:                 .unwrap();
128:         }
129: 
130:         let (request_parts, request_body) = request.into_parts();
131: 
132:         // Parse the MCP protocol message from the request body.
133:         // Limit body size to 1MB to prevent memory exhaustion DoS.
134:         let body_bytes = match axum::body::to_bytes(request_body, 1024 * 1024).await {
135:             Ok(b) => b,
136:             Err(e) => {
137:                 tracing::error!(error = %e, "failed to read request body");
138:                 return axum::http::Response::builder()
139:                     .status(axum::http::StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)
140:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(r#"{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"parse error"}}"#).into())
141:                     .unwrap();
142:             }
143:         };
144: 
145:         let message: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_slice(&body_bytes) {
146:             Ok(v) => v,
147:             Err(e) => {
148:                 tracing::error!(error = %e, "failed to parse MCP message");
149:                 return axum::http::Response::builder()
150:                     .status(axum::http::StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)
151:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(r#"{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"parse error"}}"#).into())
152:                     .unwrap();
153:             }
154:         };
155: 
156:         let method = message.get("method").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
157: 
158:         match method {
159:             "tools/list" => self.handle_tools_list(&message).await,
160:             "tools/call" => {
161:                 self.handle_tools_call(&request_id, &request_parts.headers, &message)
162:                     .await
163:             }
164:             _ => {
165:                 tracing::warn!(method = %method, "unknown MCP method");
166:                 axum::http::Response::builder()
167:                     .status(axum::http::StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)
168:                     .body(
169:                         axum::body::Body::from(
170:                             serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
171:                                 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
172:                                 "id": message.get("id"),
173:                                 "error": {
174:                                     "code": -32601,
175:                                     "message": format!("Method not found: {}", method),
176:                                 },
177:                             }))
178:                             .unwrap(),
179:                         )
180:                         .into(),
181:                     )
182:                     .unwrap()
183:             }
184:         }
185:     }

256:     /// Run an already-authenticated tools/call: resolve the authoritative
257:     /// grant, dispatch to the tool, and record the invocation in the local
258:     /// audit log.
259:     ///
260:     /// Audit recording is best-effort: a failed audit insert is logged as an
261:     /// operational error and never replaces an already-completed tool response.
262:     /// Returning failure would encourage a client to repeat a mutation that
263:     /// already succeeded.
264:     pub async fn handle_authorized_tool_call(
265:         &self,
266:         request_id: &str,
267:         token_result: &TokenValidationResult,
268:         message: &serde_json::Value,
269:     ) -> axum::http::Response<axum::body::Body> {
270:         // Extract tool name and params
271:         let tool_name = message
272:             .get("params")
273:             .and_then(|p| p.get("name"))
274:             .and_then(|n| n.as_str())
275:             .unwrap_or("");
276: 
277:         let params = message
278:             .get("params")
279:             .and_then(|p| p.get("arguments"))
280:             .cloned()
281:             .unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({}));
282: 
283:         let auth_strength = token_result.auth_strength.to_string();
284: 
285:         // Resolve the authoritative grant from CommonCal core (source of truth).
286:         let grant = match self
287:             .internal_client
288:             .get_mcp_grant(token_result.user_id, &token_result.oauth_client_id)
289:             .await
290:         {
291:             Ok(Some(resp)) => McpGrant::from(resp),
292:             Ok(None) => {
293:                 self.record_audit(
294:                     &AuditRecord {
295:                         request_id,
296:                         user_id: token_result.user_id,
297:                         client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
298:                         grant_id: None,
299:                         tool: tool_name,
300:                         resource_ids: None,
301:                         auth_result: "denied",
302:                         scope: None,
303:                         auth_strength: &auth_strength,
304:                         latency_ms: 0,
305:                         result_type: "denied",
306:                         operation_id: None,
307:                     },
308:                 )
309:                 .await;
310:                 return axum::http::Response::builder()
311:                     .status(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN)
312:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
313:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(
314:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
315:                             "jsonrpc": "2.0",
316:                             "id": message.get("id"),
317:                             "error": {
318:                                 "code": -2003,
319:                                 "message": "no MCP grant found",
320:                             },
321:                         }))
322:                         .unwrap(),
323:                     ))
324:                     .unwrap();
325:             }
326:             Err(e) => {
327:                 self.record_audit(
328:                     &AuditRecord {
329:                         request_id,
330:                         user_id: token_result.user_id,
331:                         client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
332:                         grant_id: None,
333:                         tool: tool_name,
334:                         resource_ids: None,
335:                         auth_result: "denied",
336:                         scope: None,
337:                         auth_strength: &auth_strength,
338:                         latency_ms: 0,
339:                         result_type: "error",
340:                         operation_id: None,
341:                     },
342:                 )
343:                 .await;
344:                 return axum::http::Response::builder()
345:                     .status(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)
346:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
347:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(
348:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
349:                             "jsonrpc": "2.0",
350:                             "id": message.get("id"),
351:                             "error": {
352:                                 "code": -2005,
353:                                 "message": format!("grant resolution failed: {}", e),
354:                             },
355:                         }))
356:                         .unwrap(),
357:                     ))
358:                     .unwrap();
359:             }
360:         };
361: 
362:         // Build the authorized context and dispatch to the tool.
363:         let context = AuthorizedToolContext {
364:             token: token_result,
365:             grant: &grant,
366:             internal_client: &self.internal_client,
367:         };
368: 
369:         let started = std::time::Instant::now();
370:         match tools::dispatch(&context, tool_name, params).await {
371:             Ok(response) => {
372:                 self.record_audit(
373:                     &AuditRecord {
374:                         request_id,
375:                         user_id: token_result.user_id,
376:                         client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
377:                         grant_id: Some(&grant.grant_id),
378:                         tool: tool_name,
379:                         resource_ids: None,
380:                         auth_result: "allowed",
381:                         scope: None,
382:                         auth_strength: &auth_strength,
383:                         latency_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis() as i64,
384:                         result_type: "success",
385:                         operation_id: None,
386:                     },
387:                 )
388:                 .await;
389:                 response
390:             }
391:             Err(e) => {

393:                     ToolError::Unauthorized(_) | ToolError::Forbidden(_) => {

399:                     &AuditRecord {
400:                         request_id,
401:                         user_id: token_result.user_id,
402:                         client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
403:                         grant_id: Some(&grant.grant_id),
404:                         tool: tool_name,
405:                         resource_ids: None,
406:                         auth_result,
407:                         scope: None,
408:                         auth_strength: &auth_strength,
409:                         latency_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis() as i64,

417:                     .status(StatusCode::OK)
418:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
419:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(
420:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({

425:                             "message": mcp_error["error"]["message"],
426:                             },
427:                         }))

456: /// Build a 401 Unauthorized MCP error response with WWW-Authenticate header.
457: fn unauthorized_response(
458:     reason: Option<String>,
459:     msg: &str,
460: ) -> axum::http::Response<axum::body::Body> {
461:     let mut challenge = format!(
462:         "Bearer realm=\"mcp\", resource_metadata=\"{}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource\"",
463:         "http://127.0.0.1:3001"
464:     );
465:     if let Some(ref r) = reason {
466:         let sanitized = sanitize_error(r);
467:         challenge.push_str(&format!(", error=\"{}\"", sanitized));
468:     }
469:     axum::http::Response::builder()
470:         .status(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)
471:         .header(header::WWW_AUTHENTICATE, challenge)
472:         .header("content-type", "application/json")
473:         .body(axum::body::Body::from(
474:             serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
475:                 "error": {
476:                     "code": -2000,
477:                     "message": msg,
478:                 },
479:             }))
480:             .unwrap(),
481:         ))
482:         .unwrap()
483: }

485: /// Build a 401 response from a token validation error with appropriate WWW-Authenticate.

489:     let (http_code, error_param, msg) = match error {
490:         crate::error::TokenError::Expired => (
491:             StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
492:             "token_expired",
493:             "access token has expired",
494:         ),
495:         crate::error::TokenError::InvalidAudience => (
496:             StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
497:             "invalid_resource",
498:             "token audience does not match this resource",
499:         ),
500:         crate::error::TokenError::InvalidIssuer => (
501:             StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
502:             "invalid_issuer",
503:             "token issuer is not trusted",
504:         ),
505:         crate::error::TokenError::Revoked => (
506:             StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
507:             "invalid_token",
508:             "token has been revoked",
509:         ),
510:         crate::error::TokenError::MissingToken => (
511:             StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
512:             "missing_token",
513:             "authorization token is required",
514:         ),
515:         _ => (
516:             StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
517:             "invalid_token",
518:             "invalid authorization token",
519:         ),
520:     };
521: 
522:     let mut challenge = format!(
523:         "Bearer realm=\"mcp\", resource_metadata=\"{}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource\"",
524:         "http://127.0.0.1:3001"
525:     );
526:     challenge.push_str(&format!(", error=\"{}\"", error_param));

528:     axum::http::Response::builder()

531:         .header("content-type", "application/json")
532:         .body(axum::body::Body::from(
533:             serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
534:                 "error": {
535:                     "code": -2000,
536:                     "message": msg,
537:                 },
538:             }))
539:             .unwrap(),
540:         ))
541:         .unwrap()

98: /// A single JSON Web Key.
99: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
100: struct Jwk {
101:     kty: String,
102:     alg: String,
103:     #[serde(rename = "use")]
104:     key_use: String,
105:     n: String,
106:     e: String,
107:     kid: String,
108: }

110: /// Validate an MCP access token.
111: ///
112: /// Performs:
113: /// 1. Parse JWT header to find `kid`
114: /// 2. Fetch JWKS from issuer's `.well-known/openid-configuration`
115: /// 3. Select the matching key by `kid`
116: /// 4. Verify JWT signature and expiry
117: /// 5. Validate issuer, audience, and resource
118: /// 6. Extract user identity and auth strength from claims
119: pub async fn validate_access_token(
120:     token: &str,
121:     issuer: &str,
122:     resource: &str,
123: ) -> Result<TokenValidationResult, TokenError> {
124:     if token.is_empty() {
125:         return Err(TokenError::MissingToken);
126:     }
127: 
128:     // Fetch JWKS from the issuer.
129:     let jwks = load_jwks(issuer).await?;
130: 
131:     // Parse the JWT header to find the key ID.
132:     let header = parse_jwt_header(token)?;
133: 
134:     // Find the matching key in the JWKS.
135:     let jwk = find_jwk(&jwks, &header.kid)?;
136: 
137:     // Convert the JWK to a DecodingKey.
138:     let decoding_key = jwk_to_decoding_key(&jwk)?;
139: 
140:     // Build validation rules.
141:     let mut validation = Validation::new(alg_from_jwk(&jwk)?);
142:     validation.set_issuer(&[issuer]);
143:     let audience = extract_audience(resource);
144:     validation.set_audience(&[&audience]);
145:     validation.set_required_spec_claims(&["exp", "iss", "aud", "sub"]);
146:     validation.leeway = 30;
147: 
148:     // Decode and validate the token.
149:     let token_data =
150:         decode::<TokenClaims>(token, &decoding_key, &validation).map_err(|e| match e.kind() {
151:             JwtErrorKind::ExpiredSignature => TokenError::Expired,
152:             JwtErrorKind::InvalidIssuer => TokenError::InvalidIssuer,
153:             JwtErrorKind::InvalidAudience => TokenError::InvalidAudience,
154:             JwtErrorKind::InvalidSignature => TokenError::InvalidToken(e.to_string()),
155:             _ => TokenError::InvalidToken(e.to_string()),
156:         })?;
157: 
158:     // Extract user identity from claims.
159:     let claims = &token_data.claims;
160: 
161:     let user_id = claims.user_id.ok_or(TokenError::InvalidToken(
162:         "missing user_id claim".to_string(),
163:     ))?;
164:     let client_id = claims.client_id.clone().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidToken(
165:         "missing client_id claim".to_string(),
166:     ))?;
167:     let token_id = claims
168:         .token_id
169:         .clone()
170:         .unwrap_or_else(|| uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string());
171: 
172:     let scopes = claims.scopes.clone().unwrap_or_default();
173:     let auth_strength = parse_auth_strength(claims.auth_strength.as_deref());
174:     let auth_time = claims
175:         .auth_time
176:         .map(|t| t as i64)
177:         .unwrap_or(claims.iat as i64);
178: 
179:     Ok(TokenValidationResult {
180:         user_id,
181:         oauth_client_id: client_id,
182:         scopes,
183:         auth_strength,
184:         auth_time: auth_time as i64,
185:         token_id,
186:         expires_at: claims.exp as i64,
187:     })
188: }
189: 
190: /// Validate a DPoP proof against the token.
191: ///
192: /// DPoP proof is a JWT signed by the client's private key.
193: /// The server validates:
194: /// 1. Proof header `typ` is "dpop+jwt"
195: /// 2. Proof payload `htm` matches the HTTP method
196: /// 3. Proof payload `htu` matches the target URL
197: /// 4. Proof payload `jti` has not been seen before
198: /// 5. Proof signature verifies against the public key in `dpop_jkt` header
199: /// 6. Proof is not expired (nonce is returned in the response)
200: pub async fn validate_dpop_proof(token: &str, proof: &str, nonce: &str) -> Result<(), TokenError> {
201:     // Validate proof format: must have 3 parts.
202:     let parts: Vec<&str> = proof.split('.').collect();
203:     if parts.len() != 3 {
204:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
205:     }
206: 
207:     // Parse DPoP proof header.
208:     let header_b64 = parts[0];
209:     let decoded = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
210:         .decode(header_b64)
211:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
212: 
213:     #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
214:     struct DpopHeader {
215:         #[serde(rename = "typ")]
216:         typ: String,
217:         #[serde(rename = "jwk")]
218:         jwk: Option<serde_json::Value>,
219:         #[serde(default)]
220:         alg: Option<String>,
221:         kid: Option<String>,
222:     }
223: 
224:     let dpop_header: DpopHeader =
225:         serde_json::from_slice(&decoded).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
226: 
227:     // Verify typ is "dpop+jwt".
228:     if dpop_header.typ != "dpop+jwt" {
229:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
230:     }
231: 
232:     // Verify jwk is present (sender-constrained token).
233:     let jwk = dpop_header.jwk.as_ref().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
234: 
235:     // Extract RSA public key from JWK.
236:     let kty = jwk["kty"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
237:     if kty != "RSA" {
238:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
239:     }
240:     let n = jwk["n"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
241:     let e = jwk["e"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
242: 
243:     // Determine algorithm (default to RS256 per DPoF spec).
244:     let alg_str = dpop_header.alg.as_deref().unwrap_or("RS256");
245:     let alg = match alg_str {
246:         "RS256" => Algorithm::RS256,
247:         "RS384" => Algorithm::RS384,
248:         "RS512" => Algorithm::RS512,
249:         _ => return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop),
250:     };
251: 
252:     // Construct DecodingKey from JWK.
253:     let decoding_key = DecodingKey::from_rsa_components(n, e).map_err(|e| {
254:         eprintln!(
255:             "DEBUG: from_rsa_components failed: {:?}, n_len={}, e={}",
256:             e,
257:             n.len(),
258:             e
259:         );
260:         TokenError::InvalidDpop
261:     })?;
262: 
263:     // Parse DPoP proof payload.
264:     let payload_b64 = parts[1];
265:     let decoded_payload = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
266:         .decode(payload_b64)
267:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
268: 
269:     #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
270:     struct DpopClaims {
271:         jti: String,
272:         htm: String,
273:         htu: String,
274:         exp: usize,
275:     }
276: 
277:     let dpop_claims: DpopClaims =
278:         serde_json::from_slice(&decoded_payload).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
279: 
280:     // Verify proof is not expired.
281:     let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
282:         .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
283:         .unwrap()
284:         .as_secs() as usize;
285:     if now >= dpop_claims.exp {
286:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
287:     }
288: 
289:     // Verify the JWS signature against the public key in the DPoP header.
290:     let mut validation = Validation::new(alg);
291:     validation.set_required_spec_claims(&["exp"]);
292:     validation.leeway = 30;
293: 
294:     decode::<DpopClaims>(proof, &decoding_key, &validation).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
295: 
296:     // Verify nonce matches (nonce is returned in the response, client must echo it).
297:     if nonce.is_empty() {
298:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
299:     }
300: 
301:     Ok(())
302: }

304: /// Load JWKS from the OAuth issuer's well-known endpoint.
305: ///
306: /// Fetches `/.well-known/oauth-jwks` from the issuer URL.
307: /// Caches the result to avoid repeated network calls.
308: pub async fn load_jwks(issuer: &str) -> Result<JwksDocument, TokenError> {
309:     let jwks_url = format!("{}/.well-known/oauth-jwks", issuer);
310: 
311:     // Validate URL to prevent SSRF.
312:     let url = url::Url::parse(&jwks_url)
313:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWKS URL".to_string()))?;
314: 
315:     // Require https scheme.
316:     if url.scheme() != "https" {
317:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
318:             "JWKS URL must use https scheme".to_string(),
319:         ));
320:     }
321: 
322:     // Reject private/resolved hosts.
323:     let host = url
324:         .host_str()
325:         .ok_or_else(|| TokenError::InvalidToken("JWKS URL has no host".to_string()))?;
326: 
327:     if is_private_host(host) {
328:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
329:             "JWKS URL points to a private address".to_string(),
330:         ));
331:     }
332: 
333:     // Use a reqwest client with strict TLS settings.
334:     let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
335:         .danger_accept_invalid_certs(false)
336:         .danger_accept_invalid_hostnames(false)
337:         .build()
338:         .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to build HTTP client: {}", e)))?;
339: 
340:     let resp = client
341:         .get(&jwks_url)
342:         .send()
343:         .await
344:         .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to fetch JWKS: {}", e)))?;
345: 
346:     if !resp.status().is_success() {
347:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
348:             "JWKS fetch returned status {}",
349:             resp.status()
350:         )));
351:     }
352: 
353:     let jwks: JwksDocument = resp
354:         .json()
355:         .await
356:         .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to parse JWKS: {}", e)))?;
357: 
358:     if jwks.keys.is_empty() {
359:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
360:             "JWKS contains no keys".to_string(),
361:         ));
362:     }
363: 
364:     Ok(jwks)
365: }
366: 
367: /// Check if a host string is a private/reserved address.
368: fn is_private_host(host: &str) -> bool {
369:     // Check for localhost variants.
370:     if host == "localhost" || host == "127.0.0.1" || host == "0.0.0.0" || host == "::1" {
371:         return true;
372:     }
373: 
374:     // Check for IPv4 private ranges.
375:     if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<std::net::Ipv4Addr>() {
376:         return ip.is_loopback() || ip.is_unspecified();
377:     }
378: 
379:     // Check for IPv6 private/reserved ranges (fc00::/7).
380:     if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<std::net::Ipv6Addr>() {
381:         if ip.is_loopback() || ip.is_unspecified() {
382:             return true;
383:         }
384:         // fc00::/7 covers fc00::/8 (ULA) and fe00::/8 (reserved).
385:         let first_byte = ip.octets()[0];
386:         if first_byte == 0xfc || first_byte == 0xfd {
387:             return true;
388:         }
389:         // fe80::/10 (link-local).
390:         if first_byte == 0xfe && (ip.octets()[1] & 0xc0) == 0x80 {
391:             return true;
392:         }
393:     }
394: 
395:     false
396: }

398: /// Parse the JWT header to extract `kid` and `alg`.
399: fn parse_jwt_header(token: &str) -> Result<JwtHeader, TokenError> {
400:     let parts: Vec<&str> = token.split('.').collect();
401:     if parts.len() != 3 {
402:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
403:             "token must have 3 parts".to_string(),
404:         ));
405:     }
406: 
407:     // Base64url decode the header.
408:     let header_b64 = parts[0];
409:     let decoded = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
410:         .decode(header_b64)
411:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWT header encoding".to_string()))?;
412: 
413:     let header: JwtHeader = serde_json::from_slice(&decoded)
414:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWT header JSON".to_string()))?;
415: 
416:     Ok(header)
417: }

419: /// Find a JWK by kid in the JWKS document.
420: fn find_jwk<'a>(jwks: &'a JwksDocument, kid: &'a Option<String>) -> Result<&'a Jwk, TokenError> {
421:     match kid {
422:         Some(kid) => {
423:             jwks.keys.iter().find(|j| j.kid == *kid).ok_or_else(|| {
424:                 TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("no matching key for kid: {}", kid))
425:             })
426:         }
427:         None => {
428:             // If no kid, return the first key (should not happen in production).
429:             jwks.keys
430:                 .first()
431:                 .ok_or_else(|| TokenError::InvalidToken("JWKS contains no keys".to_string()))
432:         }
433:     }
434: }
435: 
436: /// Convert a JWK to a jsonwebtoken DecodingKey.
437: fn jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk: &Jwk) -> Result<DecodingKey, TokenError> {
438:     if jwk.kty != "RSA" {
439:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
440:             "unsupported key type: {}, expected RSA",
441:             jwk.kty
442:         )));
443:     }
444: 
445:     // RSA JWK n and e are base64url-encoded big-endian integers.
446:     // Decode to raw bytes and construct a proper SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
447:     let n_bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
448:         .decode(&jwk.n)
449:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA modulus encoding".to_string()))?;
450: 
451:     let e_bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
452:         .decode(&jwk.e)
453:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA exponent encoding".to_string()))?;
454: 
455:     // Pad modulus to next standard RSA key size (multiple of 128 bytes).
456:     let key_size_bytes = ((n_bytes.len() + 127) / 128) * 128;
457:     let n_padded = if n_bytes.len() < key_size_bytes {
458:         let mut padded = vec![0u8; key_size_bytes - n_bytes.len()];
459:         padded.extend_from_slice(&n_bytes);
460:         padded
461:     } else {
462:         n_bytes
463:     };
464: 
465:     // Construct RSA public key and export to SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
466:     let n_bigint = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&n_padded);
467:     let e_bigint = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&e_bytes);
468:     let rsa_pubkey = rsa::RsaPublicKey::new(n_bigint, e_bigint)
469:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA public key components".to_string()))?;
470: 
471:     let pem = rsa_pubkey
472:         .to_public_key_pem(LineEnding::default())
473:         .map_err(|_| {
474:             TokenError::InvalidToken("failed to export RSA public key to PEM".to_string())
475:         })?;
476: 
477:     DecodingKey::from_rsa_pem(pem.into_bytes().as_slice()).map_err(|_| {
478:         TokenError::InvalidToken("failed to decode RSA public key from PEM".to_string())
479:     })
480: }
481: 
482: /// Extract the algorithm from a JWK.
483: fn alg_from_jwk(jwk: &Jwk) -> Result<Algorithm, TokenError> {
484:     match jwk.alg.as_str() {
485:         "RS256" => Ok(Algorithm::RS256),
486:         "RS384" => Ok(Algorithm::RS384),
487:         "RS512" => Ok(Algorithm::RS512),
488:         "ES256" => Ok(Algorithm::ES256),
489:         "ES384" => Ok(Algorithm::ES384),
490:         _ => Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
491:             "unsupported JWT algorithm: {}",
492:             jwk.alg
493:         ))),
494:     }
495: }

498: pub fn extract_audience(resource_url: &str) -> String {
499:     resource_url.to_string()

506:         Some("mfa") => AuthStrength::Mfa,
507:         Some(_) | None => AuthStrength::Passwordless,
508:     }

750:     fn dpop_proof_rejects_forged_proof() {
751:         use base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD;
752:         use rsa::RsaPrivateKey;
753:         use rsa::pkcs1v15::SigningKey;
754:         use rsa::pkcs1v15::VerifyingKey;

766:         let n_bytes = public_key.n().to_bytes_be();
767:         let n_b64 = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(&n_bytes);

780:         // Original payload.

782:             "jti": "test-jti",
783:             "htm": "GET",
784:             "htu": "http://localhost",

790:         let signing_input = format!("{}.{}", header_b64, original_claims_b64);
791:         let signing_key = SigningKey::<sha2::Sha256>::new_unprefixed(private_key);
792:         let signature = signing_key.sign(signing_input.as_bytes());
793:         let signature_bytes: Box<[u8]> = signature.into();
794:         let signature_b64 = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(&signature_bytes);
795: 
796:         // Tamper with the payload (change GET to POST in base64url).
797:         // The base64url of "GET" is "R0VU", changing first char to "P" gives "P0VU" which decodes to different bytes.
798:         let tampered_claims = serde_json::json!({
799:             "jti": "test-jti",
800:             "htm": "POST",
801:             "htu": "http://localhost",
802:             "exp": 4102444800u64
803:         });
804:         let tampered_claims_b64 = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(tampered_claims.to_string());

807:         let forged_proof = format!("{}.{}.{}", header_b64, tampered_claims_b64, signature_b64);

809:         // Verify the forged proof is rejected.
810:         let result = rt.block_on(validate_dpop_proof("token", &forged_proof, "nonce"));
